20	Dear Mr. Berry:
    21	From April 27 through 30, 2021 a representative of the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
    22	Administration (PHMSA), pursuant to Chapter 601 of 49 United States Code, inspected
    23	Continental Resources (Continental) records and field assets in Sydney, Montana.
    24	As a result of the inspection, it is alleged that Continental may have committed probable
    25	violations of the Pipeline Safety Regulations, Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). The
    26	items inspected and the probable violations are:
    27	1.
    28	
    29	§ 195.262 Pumping Equipment.
    30	(a) Adequate ventilation must be provided in pump station buildings to prevent the
    31	accumulation of hazardous vapors. Warning devices must be installed to warn of
    32	the presence of hazardous vapors in the pumping station building.
    33	
    34	Continental failed to install warning devices for the presence of hazardous vapor in pump station
    35	buildings. During the field asset inspection of Continental’s McKenzie, County, North Dakota
    36	Alexander Terminal facilities, PHMSA staff observed the absence of a warning device to warn
    37	of the presence of hazardous vapors in the LACT buildings.
    38	
    39	 2.
    40	
    41	§ 195.302 General Requirements.
    42	(a) Except as otherwise provided in this section and in § 195.305(b), no operator
    43	may operate a pipeline unless it has been pressure tested under this subpart without
    44	leakage. In addition, no operator may return to service a segment of pipeline that
    45	has been replaced, relocated, or otherwise changed until it has been pressure tested
    46	under this subpart without leakage.
    47	
    48	Continental operated its pipeline without first conducting a valid pressure test without leakage.
    49	Continental failed to pressure three segments of pipe for at least 4 continuous hours at a pressure
    50	of 125 percent, or more, of the maximum operating pressure and, in the case of pipeline that was
    51	not visually inspected for leakage during the test, for at least an additional 4 continuous hours at
    52	a press equal to 110 percent, or more, of the maximum operating pressure as required by
    53	§ 195.304. Specifically, On June 27, 2014, a hydrotest was completed on 328 feet of 8 inch X52
    54	pipe. On July 10, 2014 a hydrotest was completed on 490 feet of 8 inch X52 pipe. On July 18,
    55	2014 a hydrotest was completed on 24 feet of 6 inch, and 2 feet of 4 inch pipe. The duration of
    56	the hydrotests listed above were all approximately 2 hours.
    57	These hydrotests did not meet the continuous duration for lines that are not visually inspected for
    58	no leakage standard. Records showed the hydrotests were for approximately 2 hours each
    59	Therefore, Continental Resources operated these pipelines without first conducting a valid
    60	pressure test which is a violation of § 195.302(a).
    61	Proposed Civil Penalty
    62	Under 49 U.S.C. § 60122 and 49 CFR § 190.223, you are subject to a civil penalty not to exceed
    63	$239,142 per violation per day the violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,391,412 for a
    64	related series of violations. For violation occurring on or after May 3, 2021 and before March
    65	21, 2022, the maximum penalty may not exceed $225,134 per violation per day the violation
    66	persists, up to a maximum of $2,251,334 for a related series of violations.
    67	For violation occurring on or after January 11, 2021 and before May 3, 2021, the maximum
    68	penalty may not exceed $222,504 per violation per day the violation persists, up to a maximum
    69	of $2,225,034 for a related series of violations. For violation occurring on or after July 31, 2019
    70	and before January 11, 2021, the maximum penalty may not exceed $218,647 per violation per
    71	day the violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,186,465 for a related series of violations. For
    72	violation occurring on or after November 27, 2018 and before July 31, 2019, the maximum
    73	penalty may not exceed $213,268 per violation per day, with a maximum penalty not to exceed
    74	$2,132,679. For violation occurring on or after November 2, 2015 and before November 27,
    75	2018, the maximum penalty may not exceed $209,002 per violation per day, with a maximum
    76	penalty not to exceed $2,090,022.
    77	We have reviewed the circumstances and supporting documentation involved for the above
    78	probable violations and recommend that you be preliminarily assessed a civil penalty of $12,000
